questions.question: What is the purpose of BeautifulSoup in web scraping?
options: To download HTML files from the internet
To convert raw HTML strings into a searchable Python object
To render JavaScript on web pages
To automatically fill out web forms
questions.explanation: BeautifulSoup takes the messy HTML string obtained from requests and builds a structured Python object that mimics the DOM tree, making it easy to navigate and search for specific elements.

questions.question: What is the difference between `soup.find('div')` and `soup.find_all('div')`?
options: `find()` returns the first matching element; `find_all()` returns a list of all matching elements
`find()` works with tags; `find_all()` works with attributes
They are identical and can be used interchangeably
`find()` returns a string; `find_all()` returns a BeautifulSoup object
questions.explanation: `find()` returns the first matching element (a single Tag object). `find_all()` returns a list of all matching Tag objects, which you typically loop through to access each element.

questions.question: Why does BeautifulSoup use `class_` (with an underscore) instead of `class` when searching by CSS class?
options: It's a typo in the library
`class` is a reserved keyword in Python, so it cannot be used as a parameter name
The underscore makes the search faster
It only works with classes that have underscores in their names
questions.explanation: In Python, `class` is a reserved keyword used to define classes. BeautifulSoup uses `class_` (with an underscore) to avoid conflicting with this keyword when you want to search by CSS class.

questions.question: What would be the correct way to access the `href` attribute from a BeautifulSoup Tag object `link`?
questions.explanation: BeautifulSoup Tag objects behave like dictionaries. You can access attributes using square brackets: `tag['attribute_name']`.
